reason: While Yahweh is depicted as all-powerful (raining bread from heaven), the text contradicts the characterization as 'remote' and 'emotionally removed.' The passage shows direct personal engagement: Yahweh speaks to Moses with specific instructions, actively provides and tests the people, gives detailed explanations about the Sabbath, and most tellingly, expresses emotional frustration: 'How long do you refuse to keep my commandments and my laws?' (עַד־אָנָה מֵֽאַנְתֶּם לִשְׁמֹר מִצְוֺתַי וְתוֹרֹתָֽי). This rhetorical question demonstrates relational concern and emotional investment rather than remoteness. The entire passage depicts an engaged deity in active dialogue and covenant relationship with His people.
